destinations.title: Can an unstable ensemble of mixed bulk-axion KK modes reproduce the dark-matter abundance while balancing constituent abundances against lifetimes and satisfying phenomenological constraints?

How can nuclear magnetic resonance detect axion/ALP dark matter through nucleon and gluon couplings, and can frequency-modulation sidebands extend CASPEr into frequencies where resonant detection suffers from magnetometer noise?

Can a storage-ring EDM experiment detect axion-induced oscillating nucleon EDMs by tuning the g−2 spin precession into resonance, and what statistical sensitivity and frequency coverage follow under proposed beam and coherence conditions?

Can nuclear magnetic resonance detect axion/ALP dark matter through oscillating nuclear EDMs or direct spin couplings, and what materials, coherence times and readout methods support the projected CASPEr reach?

Can singular noncanonical ALP kinetic terms enlarge viable misalignment dark-matter parameter space toward stronger observable couplings, while satisfying inflationary isocurvature, QCD-induced mass and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints?

Can a confining hidden gauge sector and its associated axion jointly supply the dark matter abundance, with axions realizing fuzzy dark matter, while avoiding glueball overproduction and satisfying astrophysical and electric-dipole constraints?

Can an ultralight axion provide the observed dark matter while its long Compton wavelength suppresses small structures? Misalignment abundance ties the mass m to the decay constant f and the initial displacement θ_i.

Can coherent axion oscillations produce cold dark-photon dark matter through a tachyonic instability while visible-sector interactions eliminate the residual axion without violating cosmological constraints?

Can monodromy enlarge ALP misalignment production enough to allow stronger couplings while retaining viable dark matter, and how do resonantly amplified nonlinear fluctuations affect abundance, velocities and small-scale density structure?
Can dynamical initial conditions suppress relic overproduction by many axions and moduli while selectively producing axion dark matter and sub-Planckian axion quintessence?

Can type IIB string axions provide appreciable fuzzy dark matter through untuned initial misalignment once moduli stabilisation determines their masses and decay constants, and what compactification and observational requirements follow?

Can classical rolling of misalignment-produced axion dark matter generate observable isocurvature during low-scale inflation, and thereby impose a lower inflationary Hubble bound with distinctive correlation and spectral-index predictions?

Assuming an axion is required for each Yang–Mills group, what cosmological and observable consequences follow for dark gauge sectors? The paper studies axion abundance, inflationary isocurvature, collective dilute stars, and intersector kinetic mixing in two concrete models.

How does an electroweak-induced ALP mass contribution from an explicit shift-symmetry-breaking Higgs portal modify misalignment evolution, relic-density correlations and viable dark-matter search parameters?

Can C4 axions in explicit type IIB compactification geometries provide observable fuzzy dark matter, while avoiding heavier-axion overproduction, and what associated dark photons and cosmological signatures arise?

Can heavy string axions acquire the dark matter abundance through cosmological gravitational particle production while their associated moduli remain stabilized and the axions remain cosmologically long lived?
Can a first-order electroweak phase transition transiently accelerate one ALP enough to generate the baryon asymmetry while its subsequent oscillations account for all dark matter?

Can Gauss–Bonnet-induced delayed U(1) breaking during inflation generate a strongly scale-dependent ALP spectrum while avoiding CMB-scale isocurvature, and support dark matter, dark energy, collapsing walls or gravitational-wave scenarios?
Can bulk axion KK towers change dark-dimension dark-matter production and fragmentation enough to reconcile the relic abundance with warm-dark-matter and visible-energy-injection bounds?
Can a light axion from a high-scale, techni-anomalous global symmetry have a cosmologically acceptable misalignment abundance, satisfy diffuse x-ray constraints, and constitute dark matter?

evidence.text: Fit the tree-level neutrino matrix to the quoted oscillation best fits, add the singlet-induced correction, and evaluate changes in mass-squared differences, mixing angles and the Dirac phase while scanning its overall coupling strength.

evidence.text: Rotate the neutral η and ξ scalars into their mass eigenbasis and express the one-loop neutrino mass matrix through the Passarino–Veltman B0 function. A heavy-mediator approximation supplies an order-of-magnitude mass-scale estimate.

evidence.text: Integrate the algebraic axial torsion field in a constrained path integral, implement torsion-charge conservation with a Lagrange multiplier, and use the axial anomaly after partial integration. Counterterms are invoked to express the anomaly using the torsion-free spin connection.
